# Tasks: Product Spec Extension for Spec Kit

**Input**: Design documents from `/specs/001-product-spec-extension/`
**Prerequisites**: plan.md, spec.md, research.md, data-model.md, contracts/

**Tests**: No automated test framework was requested in the spec. The extension is verified through manual smoke runs and the per-feature quality checklist generated by the command itself. Pipeline self-tests (manifest validation, package layout, content lint) are part of the release workflow, not separate test files.

**Organization**: Tasks are grouped by user story to enable independent implementation and testing.

## Format: `[ID] [P?] [Story] Description`

- **[P]**: Can run in parallel (different files, no dependencies)
- **[Story]**: Which user story this task belongs to (US1, US2, US3, US4)
- File paths are repository-relative

## Path Conventions

This repository hosts a Spec Kit extension. Files at the repository root form the extension source plus its release tooling:

- `extension/` — canonical extension source (zipped on release).
- `extension/commands/`, `extension/templates/`, `extension/scripts/{bash,powershell}/` — extension internals.
- `catalog.json` — single-entry catalog at the repository root.
- `.github/workflows/release.yml` — release pipeline.
- `scripts/` — repository-level pipeline helper scripts.
- `.specify/extensions/product/` — optional dev-mode mirror for self-dogfooding.

## Phase 1: Setup (Shared Infrastructure)

**Purpose**: Create the directory layout and the non-code metadata files every later phase depends on.

- [ ] T001 Create the `extension/` source tree directory structure with empty placeholder dirs: `extension/`, `extension/commands/`, `extension/templates/`, `extension/scripts/bash/`, `extension/scripts/powershell/`
- [ ] T002 [P] Create `extension/LICENSE` (MIT, matching `catalog.json#license`)
- [ ] T003 [P] Create `extension/CHANGELOG.md` skeleton with an "Unreleased" section ready to receive v0.1.0 notes
- [ ] T004 [P] Create `catalog.json` at the repository root, populated with the static fields per `specs/001-product-spec-extension/contracts/catalog-entry.md` (`name`, `id`, `description`, `author`, `repository`, `license`, `tags`, `verified: false`); leave `version`, `download_url`, `created_at`, `updated_at` empty and pinned for first-release population
- [ ] T005 [P] Create the repository-level `scripts/` directory for pipeline helpers
- [ ] T006 [P] Create the `.github/workflows/` directory

## Phase 2: Foundational (Blocking Prerequisites)

**Purpose**: Author the manifest and the user-facing README. Every later user story phase reads or modifies these files, so they must exist first.

**⚠️ CRITICAL**: No user story work can begin until this phase is complete.

- [ ] T007 Author `extension/extension.yml` manifest per the schema described in `specs/001-product-spec-extension/contracts/catalog-entry.md` and the Spec Kit publishing guide: `schema_version: "1.0"`, `extension.id: product`, `extension.name: "Product Spec Extension"`, `extension.version: 0.1.0`, `extension.description`, `extension.author`, `extension.repository`, `extension.license: MIT`, `requires.speckit_version: ">=0.2.0"`, `provides.commands: [{name: speckit.product.spec, file: commands/speckit.product.spec.md, description: ...}]`, `tags: [product, spec, prd, documentation]`, `hooks: {}` (intentionally empty per FR-011)
- [ ] T008 Author `extension/README.md` skeleton with sections: Overview, Source-of-truth contract (`spec.md` is canonical, `product-spec.md` is derived), Install (three paths: `--from <url>`, catalog, `--dev`), Invoke (`/speckit-product-spec`), Style rules summary, Troubleshooting; cross-reference per FR-017, FR-023, FR-024
- [ ] T009 Create the dogfood symlink (or copy) so `.specify/extensions/product/` resolves to `extension/` in this repository, then update `.specify/extensions.yml` to add `product` under `installed`. This lets contributors run `/speckit-product-spec` against this repo's own specs.

**Checkpoint**: The extension exists as an empty but valid Spec Kit extension. It would install but does nothing useful yet. Ready to begin user story phases.

---

## Phase 3: User Story 1 — Generate product spec from existing technical spec (Priority: P1) 🎯 MVP

**Goal**: A user with a populated `spec.md` runs `/speckit-product-spec` and gets a `product-spec.md` plus a `checklists/product.md` written into the same feature directory, conforming to the canonical templates and style rules.

**Independent Test**: in a feature directory with a populated `spec.md`, run `/speckit-product-spec`. Verify both files are created, every mandatory section is populated, no implementation details leak in, no em dash appears, every Use Case scenario follows Given/When/Then with one full sentence per keyword, and every `[NEEDS CLARIFICATION]` marker from the source spec is surfaced as an open product question.

### Implementation for User Story 1

- [ ] T010 [P] [US1] Copy `specs/001-product-spec-extension/contracts/product-spec-template.md` (the Template Body section, not the wrapping contract prose) to `extension/templates/product-spec-template.md` so the runtime command can read it
- [ ] T011 [P] [US1] Copy `specs/001-product-spec-extension/contracts/quality-checklist.md` (the Template Body section) to `extension/templates/product-checklist-template.md`
- [ ] T012 [P] [US1] Author `extension/scripts/bash/resolve-feature-dir.sh`: read `.specify/feature.json#feature_directory`, verify the directory exists, exit 0 with the resolved absolute path on stdout (or non-zero with a clear error to stderr) per FR-002 and the command contract's E_NO_POINTER / E_BAD_POINTER cases
- [ ] T013 [P] [US1] Author `extension/scripts/powershell/resolve-feature-dir.ps1` as the PowerShell equivalent of T012, behavior identical, per FR-016
- [ ] T014 [US1] Author `extension/commands/speckit.product.spec.md`, the slash command body. The command MUST: invoke the resolve-feature-dir helper; refuse with a precise error when `spec.md` is missing or contains unfilled template placeholders (E_NO_SPEC, E_PLACEHOLDERS); detect non-English source spec and refuse (E_LANGUAGE); enumerate any `[NEEDS CLARIFICATION]` markers and ask the user to confirm before proceeding; detect an existing `product-spec.md` and prompt overwrite-or-abort (no merge in v1, per FR-008); read `extension/templates/product-spec-template.md` and `extension/templates/product-checklist-template.md`; instruct the AI assistant to populate the template using content drawn from the source spec, enforcing every style rule from the command contract (English only, no em dash, full-sentence Given/When/Then, no implementation detail, mandatory sections in canonical order, optional sections only when relevant); write `product-spec.md` and `checklists/product.md` to the feature directory; print a status report listing paths written, sections populated, and number of open product questions surfaced
- [ ] T015 [US1] Add to T014 the placeholder-detection logic that distinguishes unfilled `spec-template.md` placeholders (refuse) from `[NEEDS CLARIFICATION]` markers (warn-and-confirm) per FR-004
- [ ] T016 [US1] Smoke-run the command against this repo's own `specs/001-product-spec-extension/spec.md` (via the dogfood install from T009) and walk the generated `product-spec.md` through the generated `checklists/product.md`; iterate on the prompt in `extension/commands/speckit.product.spec.md` until every Required checklist item passes on the first generation. Run the smoke from three different working directories (`./specs/`, the repo root, and a sibling directory outside the repo) to verify FR-015 (working-directory independence).

**Checkpoint**: User Story 1 works end-to-end against a real source spec. The MVP is shippable for users who install the extension manually.

## Phase 4: User Story 2 — Install and discover the extension like any other Spec Kit extension (Priority: P2)

**Goal**: a Spec Kit user can drop the extension into their project and have `/speckit-product-spec` appear, without bespoke wiring, by following documented steps.

**Independent Test**: starting from a separate Spec Kit project that does not have the extension, follow the README install path (Path 3, dev install, since no release exists yet at this point in the timeline). Verify the slash command appears in the assistant, the project's `.specify/extensions/.registry` lists `product`, and existing Spec Kit lifecycle commands still pass smoke tests (per SC-007).

### Implementation for User Story 2

- [ ] T017 [P] [US2] Expand `extension/README.md` "Install — Path 3 (Developer install)" with the exact `specify extension add --dev <path-to-extension>` command, including a worked example, per FR-024
- [ ] T018 [P] [US2] Add an "Install — Path 1 (Manual copy, advanced)" section to `extension/README.md` describing the fallback for users who cannot use the CLI: copy the unpacked zip contents into `.specify/extensions/product/` and add the registry entry by hand
- [ ] T019 [US2] Run a clean-project smoke test: in a separate Spec Kit project, install via `--dev`, run `/speckit-specify` then `/speckit-product-spec`, then run `/speckit-clarify`, `/speckit-plan`, `/speckit-tasks`, `/speckit-implement` on the same feature; verify nothing breaks (SC-007). Repeat the smoke test on a project configured with `branch_numbering: timestamp` in addition to the default `sequential`, to verify FR-012 (branch-numbering passthrough).

**Checkpoint**: the extension is installable and discoverable in any Spec Kit project. Existing lifecycle commands are unaffected.

## Phase 5: User Story 4 — Publish the extension and install via `specify extension add` (Priority: P2)

**Goal**: every tag push produces a validated, deterministic release zip and an updated catalog entry, so end users install with `specify extension add product --from <url>` or `specify extension add product` (catalog).

**Independent Test**: tag a commit `v0.1.0`. Verify the GitHub Actions release pipeline runs green; a `product-0.1.0.zip` is attached to a GitHub Release at `v0.1.0`; `extension.yml` at the zip root has `version: 0.1.0`; `catalog.json#version` and `download_url` are updated on the default branch; from an unrelated Spec Kit project, `specify extension add product --from <download-url>` installs the extension and `/speckit-product-spec` is available.

### Implementation for User Story 4

- [ ] T020 [US4] Author `scripts/validate-manifest.sh`: parse `extension/extension.yml`, assert `extension.id == "product"`, assert `extension.version == ${GITHUB_REF_NAME#v}`, assert all required files exist per `specs/001-product-spec-extension/contracts/package-layout.md`, exit non-zero with a clear message on any failure
- [ ] T021 [P] [US4] Author `scripts/build-zip.sh`: read version from `extension/extension.yml`, produce `dist/product-<version>.zip` from the `extension/` subtree with files at the zip root, alphabetical entry order, file timestamps fixed to the tagged commit's timestamp; re-run `validate-manifest.sh` against the unpacked zip to catch packaging bugs; per `contracts/package-layout.md` (Determinism, Required Validation)
- [ ] T022 [P] [US4] Author `scripts/update-catalog.sh`: take `<version>` and `<download_url>` as args, update `catalog.json` fields `version`, `download_url`, `requires.speckit_version` (read from `extension/extension.yml`), `updated_at` (current ISO-8601 UTC), and `created_at` if empty; do not modify any other field; per `contracts/catalog-entry.md` (Field Rules, Pipeline Update Rules)
- [ ] T023 [P] [US4] Author `scripts/lint-content.sh`: run a markdown lint pass on all `extension/**/*.md`; assert `extension/templates/product-spec-template.md` contains no em dash outside fenced code blocks that name the rule; assert the canonical section headings appear in the canonical order; assert `extension/commands/speckit.product.spec.md` references both templates by relative path; per the lint-content job in `contracts/release-pipeline.md`
- [ ] T024 [US4] Author `.github/workflows/release.yml` with the 6 sequential jobs from `contracts/release-pipeline.md`: `validate-manifest` (runs `scripts/validate-manifest.sh`), `validate-catalog` (PR-only, blocks edits to pipeline-owned fields in `catalog.json`), `lint-content` (runs `scripts/lint-content.sh`), `build-zip` (runs `scripts/build-zip.sh`, uploads workflow artifact), `publish-release` (creates GitHub Release at the tag, attaches `product-<version>.zip`, uses the relevant `CHANGELOG.md` section as the release body), `update-catalog` (runs `scripts/update-catalog.sh`, commits to the default branch as the release-bot identity); triggers: `push.tags: ['v*.*.*']`, `pull_request: {branches: [<default>]}`, `workflow_dispatch`; the workflow MUST ignore commits authored by the release-bot identity to prevent recursive triggers
- [ ] T025 [P] [US4] Configure the release-bot identity in `.github/workflows/release.yml` (e.g. `github-actions[bot]` with a stable email) used by `update-catalog` so its commit message is `chore(release): catalog v<version>` per `contracts/catalog-entry.md`
- [ ] T026 [US4] Update `extension/README.md` "Install" section so Path 1 (Direct URL) shows the real release-asset URL pattern `https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/releases/download/v<version>/product-<version>.zip`, and Path 2 (Catalog) shows the bare `specify extension add product` command, per FR-023
- [ ] T027 [US4] Cut a v0.1.0 release: bump `extension/extension.yml#version` to `0.1.0`, write a v0.1.0 entry in `extension/CHANGELOG.md`, commit, tag `v0.1.0`, push the tag; observe the pipeline run end-to-end; verify SC-008 (clean-project install under 3 minutes), SC-009 (no release bypasses validation), SC-010 (catalog updated within 5 minutes), and SC-006 by running `/speckit-product-spec` twice in a row in the smoke project: confirm the second run shows the overwrite-or-abort prompt, confirm choosing abort leaves `product-spec.md` byte-identical (`diff -q` returns no difference)

**Checkpoint**: the extension is publicly installable. Stories 1, 2, and 4 are all live. The MVP plus distribution are complete.

## Phase 6: User Story 3 — Keep product spec and technical spec in sync (Priority: P3) — DEFERRED

User Story 3 is **explicitly deferred from v1** per the spec's Assumptions section and FR-008 (overwrite-or-abort only in v1). No tasks are generated here. A future minor or major version will introduce a refresh/diff command under the reserved `product.<verb>` namespace (e.g. `speckit.product.refresh`).

## Dependencies & Execution Order

### Phase Dependencies

- **Setup (Phase 1)**: no dependencies.
- **Foundational (Phase 2)**: depends on Setup. Blocks all user stories.
- **User Story 1 (Phase 3, MVP)**: depends on Foundational.
- **User Story 2 (Phase 4)**: depends on Foundational. Independent of US1, but the smoke test in T019 requires US1 to be complete.
- **User Story 4 (Phase 5)**: depends on Foundational. Largely independent of US1 and US2, but the v0.1.0 release in T027 cannot ship until US1 implementation (T010–T016) is in place, since the released extension must actually do something.
- **User Story 3 (Phase 6)**: deferred.
- **Polish (Phase 7)**: depends on US1, US2, and US4 being complete (T030, T031). T028 and T029 can begin earlier.

### Within Each User Story

- US1: T010, T011, T012, T013 in parallel → T014 (composes them) → T015 (extends T014) → T016 (smoke test).
- US2: T017, T018 in parallel → T019 (smoke test, requires US1 complete).
- US4: T020 → T021, T022, T023 in parallel → T024 (wires them into the workflow) → T025 (refines T024) → T026 (docs) → T027 (releases v0.1.0).

### Parallel Opportunities

- All [P] tasks in Phase 1 can run together (T002, T003, T004, T005, T006).
- US1 model-equivalent tasks T010–T013 can run together; T014 composes them sequentially.
- US2 documentation tasks T017 and T018 can run together.
- US4 helper scripts T021, T022, T023 can run together once T020 lands.
- Different developers can take US2, US4, and US3-deferred work in parallel after Phase 2 is done.

## Implementation Strategy

### MVP First (User Story 1 only)

1. Phase 1 Setup
2. Phase 2 Foundational
3. Phase 3 User Story 1 (`/speckit-product-spec` works end-to-end against a real source spec)
4. **STOP and VALIDATE**: dogfood the command on this repo's own spec; tick the generated `checklists/product.md` to confirm SC-002 and SC-003.

That alone is a useful artifact for any team who will install the extension manually.

### Incremental Delivery

1. Setup + Foundational → empty but valid extension.
2. + User Story 1 → MVP, manually installable.
3. + User Story 2 → install path documented; lifecycle smoke test green.
4. + User Story 4 → public install via `specify extension add` and a release pipeline that gates every tag.
5. + Polish → contributor docs, end-to-end quickstart, final template audit.
6. (Future) User Story 3 → refresh/diff command in a later release.

### Parallel Team Strategy

After Phase 2 is done:

- Developer A: User Story 1 (the heart of the feature; the prompt scaffolding and templates).
- Developer B: User Story 2 documentation, then User Story 4 pipeline scripts (T020–T023).
- Developer C: prep CHANGELOG and CONTRIBUTING ahead of the v0.1.0 cut.

Story 4's `T027` (the actual release) is the explicit join point; both Story 1 and Story 4 must be complete before tagging.

---

## Notes

- [P] tasks touch different files and have no dependencies on incomplete tasks.
- [Story] labels map each task to its user story for traceability.
- The release pipeline is fail-closed: any validation failure aborts the release; no partial releases are published.
- The version inside `extension/extension.yml` MUST match the git tag (without the `v` prefix); the pipeline asserts this and refuses otherwise.
- Re-tagging an already-released version is forbidden; bump the patch version instead.
- Commit after each task or logical group. The repository's `git` extension hook will offer to auto-commit at lifecycle boundaries; accept or skip per local preference.
- Stop at any checkpoint to validate the corresponding story independently against its Independent Test criterion.
